South Carolina Public Money, Sorted by Year and by Stage.

6,763 line items from state budgets, county budgets, payment reports and incentive records, checked against the government documents they cite. Each line also links to its source document.

RequestedA legislator asked for it. Not law.
AppropriatedWritten into an adopted budget.
AwardedGranted or contracted to a named recipient.
PaidMoney actually left the account.

These are different stages of the same money. Adding amounts across stages counts some dollars twice, so this page keeps a separate total for each stage.

By Year

Fiscal years run July 1 to June 30. Company incentives are grouped by the year they were approved, because the payments stretch over many years. Pick any box to open those records below.

Site Problems Found

Every source link was tested on October 1, 2026, first with an automated tool and then in a real browser where the tool was refused.

Broken, Intermittently

SC Comptroller General Vendor Payment Search

You were right that it sends people back to the home page. In 20 test searches on the state's Spending Transparency site, 9 failed. Eight landed on an "Error Page" that literally reads "No Error Found," and one bounced to the home page with no results. The same search (Palmetto Corp, FY2024-25) failed and then worked minutes later, so the server is failing, not the search terms. Monthly searches failed 6 of 10 times; yearly searches 3 of 10.

Worked (11)Failed (9)
  • Newest year is FY2024-25. FY2025-26 ended June 30, 2026 and is not in the search or the download files yet.
  • A dead link on the site itself: its "Higher Education Spending Transparency" link points to www.cg.sc.gov, a web address that no longer exists.
  • Workaround that works: the Comptroller's monthly spending files list every state payment (vendor, agency, amount, date) as downloadable spreadsheets, FY2014 through June 2025. When the search returns results, they match: Palmetto Corp shows $250,201,855 for FY2024-25.
Blocks Tools, Open to People

Dorchester, Kershaw, Richland, Berkeley

These sites refuse automated tools (error 403) but open normally in a browser. Dorchester and Kershaw both post FY2024-25 budgets, which the original research marked as unavailable.

Link Expires

Aiken County Budget Archive

The Aiken FY2024-25 budget link only works inside a short archive session, then shows "Your session Time-Out limit has been reached." Use Aiken's Financial Reporting page instead; it is linked on every Aiken record.

Transcribed

29 County Documents Posted as Scanned Images

York, Sumter, Clarendon, Chester, Chesterfield, Union, Fairfield, McCormick, Newberry, Orangeburg, Williamsburg, Colleton and Beaufort post key budget or award documents as photos of paper, which a computer can't search. All 29 have now been read twice. The first transcription's 423 entries were each checked against the scanned page (374 by text recognition, 49 by eye) with no amount differences, and the second read added one item it had missed (Fairfield's QuickJobs line, $36,798).

Were the Earmarks Paid?

Each FY2023-24 and FY2024-25 earmark was matched against every state payment in the Comptroller General's monthly spending files, July 2023 through June 2025. A match needs the earmark's own agency, that year's one-time (nonrecurring) budget fund, the amount, and a payee whose name matches. The FY2026-27 earmarks can't be checked yet: those files only run through June 2025.

ValidationThe State Treasurer publishes payment status for 32 FY2024-25 earmarks. 30 of the 32 match a payment found here. The other two (Nicholtown Community Center and River Road/Brownswood Road) are shown as "No payment found" even though the Treasurer reports them paid, because the payee or amount in the files doesn't line up cleanly; one appears to be part of a combined $1,050,000 payment to the City of Greenville.
Blind SpotThe 4 FY2023-24 earmarks paid by the State Treasurer's own office (including $4,774,000 to the City of York) don't appear anywhere in the Comptroller's files, though the Treasurer reports all 4 paid. So "No payment found" means not found in these files, not proof the money was never paid.

Source Register

Every document and page cited, with the result of the October 1, 2026 link test. The full address is shown under each title and can be selected and copied.

Built October 1, 2026 and last updated October 4, 2026 from the project's research files (prepared with ChatGPT, including a second round covering FY2023-24, Richland County and the scanned county documents), the FY2026-27 House and Senate earmark reports, SCDOT's FY2022-23 vendor payment report, and the enacted text of H.3305. The three PDFs are byte-identical to the copies online.

The House and Senate lists are requests. The enacted FY2026-27 earmarks are H.3305 (Act 261, signed September 1, 2026): 449 items totaling $349,009,298, paid in the act's priority order as money allows. Each enacted item is matched to its request by project name, so treat a match as a strong lead, not a certainty.

Statewide audited figures are in the State of South Carolina Annual Comprehensive Financial Report for the year ended June 30, 2025, which received a clean (unmodified) audit opinion from the State Auditor and Mauldin & Jenkins on January 28, 2026. It and the State Auditor's FY2025 Single Audit Report are in the source register.

Company incentive amounts are award totals. Where a disbursed figure exists, it is the total paid over the life of the grant, not spending in one year.
